---
title: "GGS-II: every country in one dataset per wave"
---

The goal: every country of GGS round 2 (GGS-II), downloaded in Stata format, and stacked into one dataset per
wave, with its labels.

## Command line

```bash
ggp-client sync
ggp-client download    --project ggs --round 2 --ext dta
ggp-client preprocess  --project ggs --round 2
ggp-client consolidate --project ggs --round 2
```

## Python

```python
import asyncio
from ggp_client import ggpClient

async def main():
    async with ggpClient(project="ggs", round=2) as p:   # data_dir defaults to "data"
        await p.sync()                                    # logs in, see Getting started
        print(len(p.rows), "files")
        print(await p.download(ext="dta"))               # (done, skipped, failed)
        print(await p.preprocess())
        print(await p.consolidate())

if __name__ == "__main__":  # needed: preprocessing runs in worker processes
    asyncio.run(main())
```

The filters are the arguments of `ggpClient`; `p.rows` holds the selected files. The steps run concurrently:
downloads several at a time, preprocessing in worker processes, consolidation as one lazy polars run.

## What you get

```
data/
├── catalogue.sqlite, .session.json, ggp_client.log
└── download/
    ├── raw/ggs-ii/w1/at/ggs2_w1_at_v1.1/.../ggsii_wave1_at_v_1_1.dta       as downloaded
    ├── processed/ggs-ii/w1/at/ggs2_w1_at_v1.1/.../ggsii_wave1_at_v_1_1.parquet
    │   processed/.../ggsii_wave1_at_v_1_1.meta.json                       its labels
    └── consolidated/ggs-ii_w1.parquet                                      all countries of wave 1
        consolidated/ggs-ii_w1.meta.json                                    their harmonized labels
        consolidated/ggs-ii_w2.parquet, ggs-ii_pilot.parquet, ...
```

In November 2026, GGS-II wave 1 was 185,660 rows from 20 countries, with 4,001 variables.

- **Preprocessing** reads each `.dta` (or `.sav`, `.csv`) once and writes it as parquet, adding the columns
  `ggp_project`, `ggp_round`, `ggp_series`, `ggp_wave`, `ggp_country`, `ggp_version` and `ggp_file` (the source).
- **Consolidating** stacks the countries by column name. A column a country lacks is empty there; a column that is
  a number in one country and text in another becomes text.
- **Country-specific variables** are left out of the consolidated file. GGS names them after the GGP country
  number, `<name>_<number><nn>`: `aut01a_2101` is Austria's (21), `a837_1401` Germany's own work schedule question
  (14). The per-country files in `processed` keep them; the log says how many were left out of which file.
- **Up to date**: preprocessing keeps existing files (`--force` redoes them). A consolidated file is rebuilt when
  its countries or input files change, for example after downloading another country.

## Both rounds, with Stata output

`python download_ggs.py` runs all of this for GGS rounds 1 and 2 and also writes every consolidated dataset as a
labelled Stata file (`ggs-ii_w1.dta`), with the harmonized variable and value labels applied. It ends with a
summary of every step and exits with 1 if anything failed.

::: {.callout-note}
Stata files are large: pyreadstat writes whole numbers as 4-byte longs and Stata stores them uncompressed.
GGS-II wave 1 is 3.3 GB as `.dta` and 36 MB as parquet; `compress` in Stata shrinks it. Text longer than 2,045
characters is cut in the `.dta`.
:::

## Known issues in the data

- Three GGS-I files (Australia waves 1 and 2, Norway wave 1) give "404 Not Found" on the portal itself.
- GGS-II Belarus wave 1 comes in English and Russian, so Belarus is in `ggs-ii_w1` twice. Filter on `ggp_file`.
- Several GGS-I files, and GGS-II Finland and Uruguay, have broken text encoding in their labels. They are read
  as latin1, which gives the same text as their `.sav` versions.
